about.title: Personal Injury Help in Fremont, California
about.longDescription: Fremont stretches from the Bay shoreline to the hills above Mission San José, and much of daily life here happens behind the wheel. Public records for 2025 list 799 injury collisions inside the city, with 1,069 people hurt and 14 lives lost. The corridors that show up most often in those counts are I-880, I-680 in both directions, and Fremont Boulevard, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to produce the highest number of reports. If one of those collisions — or a fall at a store, a dog bite, or a bike crash on your commute — has left you injured, you probably have more questions than answers right now. We handle personal injury claims in Alameda County, including those arising from vehicle collisions, falls, dog bites, and other incidents. Our team works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery. You share what happened, and we take it from there. The decision about how to proceed stays entirely with you.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Fremont Claim

items.title: The clock runs for two years — sometimes less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency may be responsible, a claim can be due in as little as six months, so getting advice early matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you share some blame for what happened, you can still pursue compensation; your share of fault reduces the amount rather than eliminating it.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For most personal injury claims in California, there is no legal ceiling on non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: Contingency fees, so cost is not a barrier
items.desc: We work on contingency. You do not pay attorney fees unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Where do injury collisions in Fremont tend to occur?
items.answer: Public collision records for Fremont show the highest counts along I-880, I-680 Southbound, Fremont Boulevard, and I-680 Northbound. Reports also cluster on Fridays between roughly 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are simply counts from public data reflecting high traffic volume, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Fremont?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. If a government entity is involved — for example, a city vehicle or a poorly maintained public road — you may need to file a claim within six months. Because these deadlines vary, it is worth speaking with an attorney as soon as you are able.

items.question: Do you charge me anything?
items.answer: No. Our services are free. We handle personal injury claims serving Alameda County, and we work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you are not barred from pursuing a claim. We can help evaluate how fault might be assigned in your situation.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary California personal injury cases, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and emotional distress. The amount depends on the specific facts of your case. We can walk you through what is realistic for your circumstances without making promises.
